messages:
maya: quick heads-up — perf-regression spike on A100 pools after yesterday's kernel selector change. 99p latency for generation workloads jumped ~30% for mid-size prompts (512-1024).
jon: saw that in dashboards too. cost per token up ~12% for A100. where's the hotspot?
maya: profiler shows more frequent fallback to the generic attention kernel for layers >30 when seq>512. KV fragmentation also higher (more cache evictions). trace attached to infra ticket.
hannah: hmm sounds like our kernel-fit heuristic misranked optimized kernels for those sequence-lengths. did the selector weights change?
jon: weight tweak landed in canary — lowered priority of 'kv-friendly' kernel in tie-breaker. it seemed fine during microbenchmarks but real traffic distribution differs.
liam: real-traffic histograms: A100 pools had a bimodal seq distribution (64 & 768). continuous-batching glued smaller requests but started aggregating more 768s together -> batch token totals hit old max_batch_tokens ceiling and pushed kernel choice to a safe path.
kai: any difference across cards? A10/T4/L4 behaved normally?
maya: L4 & T4 stable. A10 had slightly higher tail thanks to packing efficiency; H100 unaffected. only A100 saw both kernel fallback and KV cache churn.
jon: propose: switch from a static max_tokens_per_batch per-card to a dynamic per-card token budget computed from 3 inputs: memory headroom, recent kernel-fit score, and seq-length histogram. algorithm sketch below.
maya: sounds good. can you paste the sketch?
jon: ```
// per-card dynamic budget (tokens)
base = card_max_tokens_static // current default
mem_factor = clamp(available_mem / total_mem, 0.2, 1.0)
kernel_factor = sigmoid(kernel_fit_score) // higher when optimized kernels served
hist_factor = 1 - p95_long_seq_fraction // penalize cards with many long sequences
new_budget = floor(base * mem_factor * kernel_factor * hist_factor)
// enforce min/max per-card safeties
new_budget = clamp(new_budget, min_tokens, max_tokens_global)
```
liam: kernel_fit_score — is that from our offline kernel profiler or measured on live traffic?
jon: combination: rolling-window on live selected-kernel success (did we use optimized kernel without fallback) + periodic offline microbenchmarks to calibrate the sigmoid mapping.
hannah: we should also consider KV fragmentation metric. when we reduce budget too aggressively we increase small-batch churn and KV fragmentation. maybe include a kv_fragmentation_penalty.
kai: good point. add kv_penalty = 1 - min(0.5, kv_fragmentation_rate / target_rate) to hist_factor multiplication.
maya: agree. objective: minimize p99 latency while keeping cost neutral. operational constraints: no abrupt budget swings during peak. we need smoothing.
jon: plan: 2-phase rollout
1) simulation: replay 48h production trace to compute per-card budgets and predicted kernel-fit + latency.
2) canary: apply dynamic budgets to 10% A100 capacity with smoothing window=30m.
3) monitor latency, kernel-fallback-rate, kv-evictions. abort if p99 regresses >5% or fallback_rate up >10pp.
liam: do we need a fallback policy for cross-card routing? e.g., route to A10 when A100 budget throttles? routing costs differ.
hannah: let's keep routing unchanged for now; prefer internal handling by batch formation and kernel chooser. cross-card routing adds more variables.
kai: what about a quick config patch to raise max_batch_tokens on A100 slightly while we tune? temporary mitigation?
maya: risky — raising max_tokens caused the initial packing to group many 768s and triggered the fallback. but a modest increase plus kv_penalty could help. maybe +10% with monitoring.
jon: I'll prepare the replay job and a simulation dashboard. can someone own the canary rollout instrumentation? need per-card: p50/p95/p99, kernel-fallback-rate, kv-evictions/sec, cost/tok.
hannah: I can own canary instrumentation + alert playbook. will add a Grafana panel and set auto-alerts.
liam: I'll run the replay and produce the initial per-gpu budget table. output will include suggested base, mem_factor avg, kernel_fit_score, kv_fragmentation_rate, proposed_budget.
maya: thanks. timeline?
jon: replay results by EOD tomorrow, canary config ready in 24h after that. hannah will have dashboards before canary.
perf-bot: automated note: started replay job 1766543210-1 by liam. ETA ~14h. track: infra/replay/1766543210.
maya: perfect. one more ask — include model-size dimension; 7B vs 70B have different kernel-fit behavior. tag budgets per model-family where feasible.
liam: noted, will split budgets in replay by model_family label.
jon: thanks team. we'll iterate on kernel selector weights after we see replay results; aim to restore p99 to pre-change baseline. :thumbsup:
maya: ack. if anything spikes during canary ping immediately on #eng-oncall and escalate.
hannah: will prepare rollback runbook and add runbook snippet to alert.
maya: closing for now.
thread_summary: A100 p99 regression after kernel selector tweak; team proposes dynamic per-card token budgets combining memory headroom, kernel-fit score, seq histograms and KV fragmentation; plan = replay -> canary -> monitor, with instrumentation owner and rollout criteria.
